text:
morgan: quick heads-up — I ran a perf sweep after the new activation-checkpointing change and hit weird all-reduce spikes during PP stage boundaries. overall throughput down ~12% on 8xA100. cc @kevin @anika
kevin: can you paste the profiler flame or counters? is this during forward or recompute window?
man: it's during recompute (remat) windows — seems tied to checkpointed layers crossing TP/PP boundaries. attaching condensed counters:```
ALLREDUCE ms: [base: 0.9, normal: 1.1, remat-spike: 2.6]
GPU utilization: [core: 68%, avg: 62%]
KV cache hit rate: 97% (no change)
Batching: avg batch size 6 -> 6 (unchanged)
```
anika: interesting that kv cache didn't move. could be that recompute changes micro-timing and forces smaller effective overlap, so allreduce waits pile up. did you see more small allreduces (N=many small collectives) or single big ones?
morgan: more small ones — the per-layer grads become fragmented because remat causes staggered recompute ordering. i profiled NCCL ops and saw lots of ~200-400us allreduces instead of the usual 1-2ms consolidated ops.
lia: that fragmentation matches what we saw in the batching heuristics PR a while back where small per-worker tensors prevented kernel coalescing. are kernel selection paths picking narrow kernels for these shapes?
kevin: @morgan can you dump kernel choices for a representative step? prefix with layer idx and tp/pp coords. also what autotuner profile did you use (legacy vs new-kernel-router)?
man: here's an excerpt:```
layer 42 tp0/pp1: matmul kernel=gemm_small_fast (wandb: chosen)
layer 43 tp1/pp1: matmul kernel=gemm_wide (fallback)
collective ops: many NCCL allreduce size 64KB x 18 ops
```
anika: 64KB x18 explains the latency cliff — small sized allreduces have poor bandwidth and high startup. if remat creates 18 fragmented grads we get startup*18. need consolidate.
lia: possible mitigations: 1) adjust recompute schedule to align boundaries so grads aggregate before allreduce, 2) add a pre-allreduce coalesce pass in runtime that buffers small grads for up to X us (micro-batching of collectives), 3) tune kernel selector to pick kernels that produce fewer fragmented grad tensors (bigger fused outputs).
kevin: option 2 seems lowest risk. we already have a deferrable-collectives queue for KV cache invalidations, could extend that to gradient collects with a hard timeout (e.g., 250us). tradeoff is added latency tail for single-request SLOs.
man: i tested a crude buffer with 200us window on a dev rig: allreduce op count dropped from 18->4 and p99 latency improved ~1.4x but p50 increased by ~40us. for batchy workloads p99 win is worth it.
perf-bot: perf alert created: perf-1842109999 -> tags: remat, allreduce, pp-tp, kvcache-unchanged
anika: curious about KV cache modes — does the runtime switch KV layout or replicate? because if remat delays KV writes it could interfere with pipeline overlap heuristics even if hit rate is same.
man: KV writes still follow write-through layout, but the recompute timing mean we launch recompute kernels later, so the pipeline stage scheduling causes collectives to line up more often. basically timing shift not cache miss.
kevin: plan of action: 1) add micro-coalesce collectives prototype (kevin) 2) add a remat alignment test to scheduler (morgan + anika) 3) run full 8x sweep with kernel-router:new on Monday (lia). i'll open issues and link tests.
man: opened issue #3421 with logs and NCCL traces, marked p1 for performance regressions. thanks all. :thumbsup:
kevin: also add an experiment to toggle checkpoint granularity (group layers into checkpoint blocks) — maybe bigger blocks reduce fragmentation.
anika: noted. i'll try group sizes 4/8 and measure allreduce counts.
lia: if you want, i can prototype a runtime flag `collective_coalesce_us` default 0 for off, start with 200.
man: yes please. let's keep it toggled off by default until we evaluate SLO impact.
